rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act - Foreclosure Tenant Protections
rules.requirement: If a rental property is foreclosed, the new owner must give tenants at least 90 days' notice to quit before evicting them to occupy the unit personally, and foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental units; applies even to month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units.
rules.exemptions: Month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units are not exempt from the 90-day notice requirement.
rules.quoted_span: Before a tenant can be evicted due to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t when the foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her primary residence.

rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act - Good Cause Eviction / Relocation Assistance
rules.requirement: Landlords may only evict tenants for specific legal causes listed in state law (e.g., redevelopment, illegal occupancy); for certain no-fault causes like property being taken off the market for redevelopment, the landlord must serve a Notice to Quit at least three months before filing suit and provide relocation assistance before the tenant can be evicted.
rules.key_value: 3-month Notice to Quit; relocation assistance equal to 6 times monthly rent for illegal occupancy evictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential tenancies in New Jersey subject to the Anti-Eviction Act's listed causes.
rules.penalty: Landlord required to repay relocation fund money to municipality; 18% annual interest accrues on unpaid relocation balance if not timely paid.
rules.quoted_span:
A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit 
for eviction. The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.

rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act - Stay of Eviction / Self-Help Eviction Ban
rules.requirement: Tenants may request a court stay of eviction for up to one year due to special circumstances, and landlords are prohibited from using self-help evictions or lockouts to remove tenants without a court judgment.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential tenancies in New Jersey.
rules.penalty: Landlord may be charged with disorderly conduct for illegal self-help eviction/lockout.
rules.quoted_span:
“Self-help” eviction is entry into a dwelling unit and removal of tenants without their 
consent or without a judgment from a court, are  not permitted in New Jersey under any 
circumstances.
